newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech cen bank targets 1997 M2 growth at 8-12 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech cen bank targets 1997 M2 growth at 8-12 pct.

text.p: The Czech central bank (CNB) on Thursday said its target range for growth in the key M2 money supply measure was between 8-12 percent.
The CNB added in a statement that it saw year-on-year inflation at the end of 1997 dipping to below eight percent if the government met the price deregulation targets it had set.
It said the "main (economic) risk for the coming period" was the current growth in wages, which was outpacing the increase in industrial output.

"The council also forecasts that if the government holds its intended extent of changes of regulated prices, the year-on-year increase of consumer prices will be below eight percent," the statement added.
Czech year-on-year inflation ended 1996 at 8.6 percent.
The statement said the 1996 results were more or less in line with original expectations.
But it said the main risk for the period ahead was the prevailing growth of wages that outpaced productivity, "which also influences the unsatisfactory development of the current account".
The Czech current account was in deficit by some $3.1 billion for the first nine months of 1996, while the capital account surplus was $2.0 billion.
